# cards: listing
# 1 + 2 + ... + n, for the n on the card. TS 20 counts down and TS 21
# holds the total. DISCRIM chooses the way on: back round while TS 20
# still has a digit in it, out when it has none.
TOTAL
  1   P, DL 2
  2   DL 2,1 - TS 20
  4   CLEAR TS 21
 10   TS 21 - TS 2;  ADD 'A';  TS 20 - TS 2;  ADD;  TS 4 - TS 21
      TS 20 - TS 2;  ADD 'A';  TOTAL 60 - TS 2;  SUBTRACT;  TS 4 - TS 20
      TS 20 - TS 9;  TS 20 - TS 10;  AND
      TOTAL 61 - TS 15;  TOTAL 62 - TS 16
      B, BURY;  B, DISCRIM;  TS 24 - TS 6;  B, 1
 50   TS 21 - TS 13
 52   B, BURY
 53   B, BINDEC
 54   O, DL 10
 55   B, TOTAL 55
# The numbers: 1, and the two ways on.
 60   +1
 61   B, TOTAL 10
 62   B, TOTAL 50

examples.name: gcd
examples.program:
# cards: listing
# Euclid by subtraction: the greatest common divisor of the two numbers on
# the card. There is no division (section 12 makes it an instruction table
# operation), so the larger is reduced by the smaller until they are equal.
# The sign of a - b is read from TS 5, which is all ones when the partial
# sum is negative, and DISCRIM chooses the way on.
GCD
  1   P, DL 2
  2   DL 2,1 - TS 20
  4   DL 2,2 - TS 21
# Equal? a - b has no digit 1.
 10   TS 20 - TS 2;  ADD 'A';  TS 21 - TS 2;  SUBTRACT
      TS 4 - TS 9;  TS 4 - TS 10;  AND
      GCD 161 - TS 15;  GCD 160 - TS 16
      B, BURY;  B, DISCRIM;  TS 24 - TS 6;  B, 1
# Negative? Then b is the larger.
 40   TS 20 - TS 2;  ADD 'A';  TS 21 - TS 2;  SUBTRACT
      TS 5 - TS 9;  TS 5 - TS 10;  AND
      GCD 163 - TS 15;  GCD 162 - TS 16
      B, BURY;  B, DISCRIM;  TS 24 - TS 6;  B, 1
# a = a - b
100   TS 20 - TS 2;  ADD 'A';  TS 21 - TS 2;  SUBTRACT;  TS 4 - TS 20;  B, GCD 10
# b = b - a
120   TS 21 - TS 2;  ADD 'A';  TS 20 - TS 2;  SUBTRACT;  TS 4 - TS 21;  B, GCD 10
140   TS 20 - TS 13;  B, BURY;  B, BINDEC;  O, DL 10
146   B, GCD 146
# The ways on.
160   B, GCD 140
161   B, GCD 40
162   B, GCD 100
163   B, GCD 120

examples.name: blank
examples.program:
# A completely blank instruction has a definite meaning (section 12): pass
# the material on the card in the reader into DL 0. Turing arranged that the
# order the machine starts with is 0 throughout, so that it reads its first
# card without being told.
#
# Here the blank instruction is written as 32 zeros, and the card it reads
# is punched again.
START
  1   0000,0000,0000,0000,0000,0000,0000,0000
  2   O, DL 0
  3   B, START 3

examples.name: countdown
examples.program:
# cards: listing
# Count down from the number on the card to 1, one card each. The way on is
# chosen by DISCRIM: back round while TS 20 has a digit in it.
COUNT
  1   P, DL 2
  2   DL 2,1 - TS 20
 10   TS 20 - TS 13;  B, BURY;  B, BINDEC;  O, DL 10
      TS 20 - TS 2;  ADD 'A';  COUNT 60 - TS 2;  SUBTRACT;  TS 4 - TS 20
      TS 20 - TS 9;  TS 20 - TS 10;  AND
      COUNT 61 - TS 15;  COUNT 62 - TS 16
      B, BURY;  B, DISCRIM;  TS 24 - TS 6;  B, 1
 50   B, COUNT 50
# The numbers: 1, and the two ways on.
 60   +1
 61   B, COUNT 10
 62   B, COUNT 50

examples.program:

ECHO

  2   O, DL 2
  3   B, ECHO 3

examples.name: from-ts6
examples.program:
# An instruction can be obeyed from TS 6 (section 11). B with a 1 in
# column 17 carries out whatever is in TS 6, and if that is of type A the
# machine goes on at the instruction after the B. Here the instruction is
# made by the program: Q puts a position into digits 17-32 of TS 6, and the
# code of type O is added to digits 1-16 by OR. Q leaves digits 1-16 of TS 6
# as they were, so TS 6 is cleared first.
MAKE
  1   NEVER
  2   TS 8 - TS 6
  3   Q, DL 7,1
  4   TS 6 - TS 9
  5   MAKE 20 - TS 10
  7   OR
  8   TS 8 - TS 6
  9   B, 1
 10   B, MAKE 10
# The code of type O, digits 5-8 = 0001.
 20   0000,0001,0000,0000,0000,0000,0000,0000

DL 7,1  +7
DL 7,2  +1

examples.name: logic
examples.program:
# The five logical operations of section 12 work digit by digit on TS 9
# and TS 10 and leave the result in TS 8. Each result is punched as a row
# of the card, so the holes show the digits.
LOGIC
  1   DL 1,1 - TS 9
  3   DL 1,2 - TS 10
  5   AND;   TS 8 - DL 2,1
  8   OR;    TS 8 - DL 2,2
 11   NOT;   TS 8 - DL 2,3
 14   IFF;   TS 8 - DL 2,4
 17   NEVER; TS 8 - DL 2,5
 20   O, DL 2
 21   B, LOGIC 21

DL 1,1  1100,0000,0000,0000,0000,0000,0000,0000
DL 1,2  1010,0000,0000,0000,0000,0000,0000,0000

examples.name: short-multiplication
examples.program:
# cards: listing
# Short multiplication: a multiplier less than 16 written in the
# instruction itself (GIV), from Fig. 37. S, POS, CANCEL, GIV, 6 is six
# times TS 2. SELF multiplies the partial sum by itself instead, so
# S, POS, CANCEL, SELF, GIV, 6 makes it six times larger again.
SHORT
  1   P, DL 2
  2   DL 2,1 - TS 2
  4   S, POS, CANCEL, GIV, 6
  5   S, POS, CANCEL, SELF, GIV, 6
  6   TS 4 - TS 13
  8   B, BURY
  9   B, BINDEC
 10   O, DL 10
 11   B, SHORT 11

examples.name: tpk
examples.program:
# cards: listing
# TPK, the algorithm Knuth and Trabb Pardo wrote in some twenty early
# languages (D. E. Knuth and L. Trabb Pardo, "The Early Development of
# Programming Languages", Stanford STAN-CS-76-562, 1976, p. 3), written as
# an instruction table for the ACE of 1945. Their ALGOL 60:
#
#   TPK: begin integer i; real y; real array a[0:10];
#     real procedure f(t); real t; value t;
#       f := sqrt(abs(t)) + 5 x t ^ 3;
#     for i := 0 step 1 until 10 do read(a[i]);
#     for i := 10 step -1 until 0 do
#     begin y := f(a[i]);
#       if y > 400 then write(i, "TOO LARGE")
#       else write(i, y);
#     end
#   end.
#
# The input is one card of eleven whole numbers, a0 to a10. The output is
# 22 cards, i then f(a[i]) or 999, for i = 10 down to 0.
#
# What had to change, and why:
# - Whole numbers. The report's arithmetical code of two minor cycles,
#   2^m x beta with an error (section 4), is described but MULTIP and ADD,
#   the tables that would work in it, are not printed; the library's do
#   whole numbers only. So, by Knuth and Trabb Pardo's rule for such
#   languages (pp. 4-5), the a[i] are whole numbers and sqrt is the largest
#   whole number whose square is not more than its argument.
# - 999 for TOO LARGE. Cards come out as BINDEC leaves them in DL 10,
#   digits in columns (section 13); the report gives no letters.
# - One card per value: BINDEC puts one number on a card, so write(i, y)
#   becomes two cards, and the output is the 22 values b0 to b21 of Knuth
#   and Trabb Pardo's rule.
# - read(a[i]) is one card: P, DL 2 reads twelve numbers at once into DL 2,1
#   to DL 2,12, so a[i] is in DL 2,i+1. It is fetched by INDEXIN, with a
#   whole order of type L in TS 27, as CALPOL calls it; TS 27 is moved back
#   one minor cycle each time round, the reverse of PLUSIND.
# - The square root. The report has no table for it and says only that
#   division is an ITO (section 12, p. 27). SQROOT is ours: it takes away
#   1, 3, 5, ... and counts, needing no division.
# - f is a subsidiary, F, entered with B, BURY; B, F and left by B, UNBURY
#   (sections 6 and 13). Its argument is in TS 13 and its value comes back
#   in TS 25, the storages CALPOL uses for its argument and result.
# - 5 x t^3: t^3 by MULTIP twice with TRANS 45 between, as CALPOL does;
#   5 x by short multiplication, a single instruction (section 4).
# - y > 400 is asked as "is 400 - y negative?": TS 5 is all ones after a
#   subtraction that comes out negative, and DISCRIM chooses the way on.
# - It needs two of the corrections `ace errata` lists: `half` in INDEXIN,
#   and `sign` in DISCRIM, because both questions it asks put a word of all
#   ones in TS 8. With `--errata none` it never stops.
#
# TS 29 is i, TS 27 the order that fetches a[i], TS 25 is y.
TPK
  1   P, DL 2
  2   TPK 200 - TS 27;  TPK 201 - TS 29
# y := f(a[i])
 10   B, BURY;  B, INDEXIN;  TS 28 - TS 13
      B, BURY;  B, F
# write i
      TS 29 - TS 13;  B, BURY;  B, BINDEC;  O, DL 10
# y > 400?
      TPK 202 - TS 2;  ADD 'A';  TS 25 - TS 2;  SUBTRACT
      TS 5 - TS 9;  TS 5 - TS 10;  AND
      TPK 203 - TS 15;  TPK 204 - TS 16
      B, BURY;  B, DISCRIM;  TS 24 - TS 6;  B, 1
# TOO LARGE: 999 in place of y.
 60   TPK 205 - TS 25
# write y
 62   TS 25 - TS 13;  B, BURY;  B, BINDEC;  O, DL 10
# Back one minor cycle, i := i - 1, and round again unless i is negative.
      TS 27 - TS 2;  ADD 'A';  TPK 207 - TS 2;  SUBTRACT;  TS 4 - TS 27
      TS 29 - TS 2;  ADD 'A';  TPK 206 - TS 2;  SUBTRACT;  TS 4 - TS 29
      TS 5 - TS 9;  TS 5 - TS 10;  AND
      TPK 208 - TS 15;  TPK 209 - TS 16
      B, BURY;  B, DISCRIM;  TS 24 - TS 6;  B, 1
150   B, TPK 150
# The numbers: the order that fetches a10; 10; 400; the two ways on from
# y > 400; 999; 1; a pulse in digit 18, one minor cycle; and the two ways
# on at the end of the loop.
200   L, DL 2,11
201   +10
202   +400
203   B, TPK 60
204   B, TPK 62
205   +999
206   +1
207   0000,0000,0000,0000,0100,0000,0000,0000
208   B, TPK 150
209   B, TPK 10

# F (General Description). The value of sqrt|t| + 5 t^3 for the whole
# number t in TS 13 is put into TS 25, sqrt being the largest whole number
# whose square is not more than |t|. TS 2-6, 8-10, 15, 16, 18-24 are
# altered.
F
# |t|: s = TS 5 is all ones if t is negative; (t with every digit changed
# where s has a 1) - s.
  1   TS 13 - TS 2;  ADD 'A';  TS 5 - TS 19
      TS 13 - TS 9;  TS 19 - TS 10;  IFF;  TS 8 - TS 10;  NOT
      TS 8 - TS 2;  ADD 'A';  TS 19 - TS 2;  SUBTRACT;  TS 4 - TS 18
      B, BURY;  B, SQROOT;  TS 22 - TS 25
# t^3, by MULTIP twice: TS 18 times TS 20 into TS 22.
      TS 13 - TS 18;  TS 13 - TS 20;  B, BURY;  B, MULTIP
      B, BURY;  B, TRANS 45;  B, BURY;  B, MULTIP
# 5 t^3 by short multiplication, and the root added by ADD.
      TS 22 - TS 2;  S, POS, CANCEL, GIV, 5;  TS 4 - TS 18
      TS 25 - TS 20;  B, BURY;  B, ADD;  TS 22 - TS 25
      B, UNBURY

# SQROOT (General Description). The largest whole number whose square is
# not more than the whole number in TS 18, which must not be negative, is
# put into TS 22. TS 2-6, 8-10, 15, 16, 18, 19 and 24 are altered.
#
# Outline of operation. 1, 3, 5, ... are taken from TS 18 in turn, the
# next odd number being kept in TS 19, until what is left would be
# negative. How many were taken away is the root: 1 + 3 + ... + (2r - 1)
# is r squared.
SQROOT
  1   CLEAR TS 22
  4   SQROOT 60 - TS 19
 10   TS 18 - TS 2;  ADD 'A';  TS 19 - TS 2;  SUBTRACT;  TS 4 - TS 18
      TS 5 - TS 9;  TS 5 - TS 10;  AND
      SQROOT 62 - TS 15;  SQROOT 61 - TS 16
      B, BURY;  B, DISCRIM;  TS 24 - TS 6;  B, 1
# Not negative: count one, and the next odd number.
 40   TS 22 - TS 2;  ADD 'A';  SQROOT 60 - TS 2;  ADD;  TS 4 - TS 22
      TS 19 - TS 2;  ADD 'A';  SQROOT 63 - TS 2;  ADD;  TS 4 - TS 19
      B, SQROOT 10
 59   B, UNBURY
# The numbers: 1; the two ways on; 2.
 60   +1
 61   B, SQROOT 40
 62   B, SQROOT 59
 63   +2

  5   DL 5,9 - TS 22
  7   DL 5,13 - TS 23
  9   B, UNPLACED 9
